items.title: Unit, time and spectral correspondence between the physical scattering operators and the nondimensional Laplacian
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $m,\hbar>0$, put
$c:=\hbar^{2}/(2m)$, let $\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) in dimension $d=3$, let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be measurable
and put $W:=V/c$. For a measurable $U$ let $M_U$ be the maximal
multiplication operator on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, with
$D(M_U):=\{f\in L^2:Uf\in L^2\}$ and $M_Uf:=Uf$. Write
$$A_{0}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{4\pi^{2}|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad D(A_{0}):=\bigl\{f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C):|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\bigr\},$$
$$A:=A_{0}+M_{W},\quad D(A):=D(A_{0}),\qquad H_{0}:=cA_{0},\qquad H:=cA=cA_{0}+M_{V}.$$
$D(A_{0})\subseteq D(M_V)=D(M_W)$ is assumed, and assume that
$A=A_0+M_W$ is self-adjoint on $D(A_0)$. These two hypotheses hold
automatically for real bounded measurable $V$ by
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clauses (a),(c), so every original bounded-potential case is retained.
So $A_{0}$ is the operator $-\Delta_{w}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] and
$D(A_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). For a self-adjoint operator $T$ write
$E_{T}$ for the regular projection valued measure of
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] and
$\mu^{T}_{\psi}(B):=\langle E_{T}(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ for $\psi\in L^{2}$. Then:

(a) $A$ and $H$ are self-adjoint with domain $D(A)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$,
and $H=cA$ and $H_{0}=cA_{0}$ hold as operator identities on that common domain;

(b) for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$E_{H}(cB)=E_{A}(B),\qquad E_{H_{0}}(cB)=E_{A_{0}}(B);$$
consequently $\mu^{H}_{\psi}(cB)=\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)$ for every $\psi$ and every
Borel $B$, and $\sigma(H)=c\,\sigma(A)$, $\sigma(H_{0})=c\,\sigma(A_{0})$;

(c) for every $t\in\mathbb R$, with $\tau:=\hbar t/(2m)=\frac{tc}{\hbar}$,
$$e^{-itH/\hbar}=e^{-i\tau A},\qquad e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}=e^{-i\tau A_{0}},$$
where the exponentials are those of
[[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]];

(d) let $F:\mathbb R\to\mathcal B(L^{2})$ be any family of bounded operators and
$\tau(t):=\hbar t/(2m)$. For every $\psi\in L^{2}$ the strong limit
$\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}F(\tau(t))\psi$ exists if and only if
$\lim_{\tau\to\pm\infty}F(\tau)\psi$ exists, and then the two limits are equal;
in particular
$$\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar} =\operatorname*{s-lim}_{\tau\to\pm\infty}e^{i\tau A}e^{-i\tau A_{0}}$$
in the sense that either strong limit exists exactly when the other does, and
then they are equal;

(e) $\mu^{H}_{\psi}$ is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure
if and only if $\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is, and likewise for singularity with respect
to Lebesgue measure and for absence of atoms; and $\psi\ne0$ is an eigenvector
of $H$ with eigenvalue $\lambda$ if and only if it is an eigenvector of $A$
with eigenvalue $\lambda/c$.

The statement is an operator identity and a statement about spectral measures;
no physical interpretation, no scattering limit and no cross section is
asserted.

items.title: The three-dimensional continuity identity, the vanishing stationary divergence and the incident and outgoing current readings
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$m,\hbar>0$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$ and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be
nonempty open sets ([[def-interval]]), and let
$u,v:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ be functions of class $C^{2}$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) that satisfy the two real
equations
$$\hbar\,\partial_{t}u=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta v+Vv,\qquad -\hbar\,\partial_{t}v=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta u+Vu$$
pointwise on $\Omega\times I$ for a real-valued function $V$ on $\Omega\times
I$, where $\Delta=\partial_{1}^{2}+\partial_{2}^{2}+\partial_{3}^{2}$
([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]) and where the equations are the
componentwise reading of
$i\hbar\,\partial_{t}\psi=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\psi+V\psi$ for
$\psi:=u+iv$. Put
$$n:=u^{2}+v^{2}:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R,\qquad \mathbf j:=\frac{\hbar}{m}\bigl(u\,\nabla v-v\,\nabla u\bigr):\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^{3},$$
with $\nabla$ the gradient of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] and
$\operatorname{div}$ the divergence of
[[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]. Then:

(a) *Continuity identity.* $\partial_{t}n+\operatorname{div}\mathbf j=0$
pointwise on $\Omega\times I$.

(b) *Stationary solutions.* If $u,v:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ are $C^{2}$ and
independent of $t$, if $V:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is real, and if there is a real
$E$ with
$$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta u+Vu=Eu,\qquad -\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta v+Vv=Ev$$
pointwise on $\Omega$, then $\operatorname{div}\mathbf j=0$ on $\Omega$ for the
time-independent field $\mathbf j=\frac{\hbar}{m}(u\nabla v-v\nabla u)$, and for
every closed ball $\overline{B(a,r)}\subseteq\Omega$ with outward unit normal
$\nu$ on the sphere $\partial B(a,r)$,
$$\int_{\partial B(a,r)}\mathbf j\cdot\nu\,dS=0 .$$

(c) *The two explicit readings.* Let $k>0$, $d\in S^{2}$ and define
$u(x):=\cos(kd\cdot x)$, $v(x):=\sin(kd\cdot x)$ on $\Omega=\mathbb R^{3}$
(then $u,v$ are $C^{\infty}$ and satisfy the stationary equations with $V=0$,
$E=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)$). Then
$$\mathbf j=\frac{\hbar k}{m}\,d\qquad\text{on }\mathbb R^{3}.$$
Let $r_{0}>0$, write $\Omega:=\{x\in\mathbb R^{3}:|x|>r_{0}\}$, let
$\Omega\ni x=r\,\omega$ with $r=|x|$, $\omega\in S^{2}$, and let
$a,b:S^{2}\to\mathbb R$ be functions with $a,b\in C^{1}$; define
$$u(x):=\frac{a(\omega)\cos(kr)-b(\omega)\sin(kr)}{r},\qquad v(x):=\frac{a(\omega)\sin(kr)+b(\omega)\cos(kr)}{r}$$
on $\Omega$, so that $u+iv=\frac{f(\omega)}{r}e^{ikr}$ with $f:=a+ib$. Then
$u,v\in C^{1}(\Omega)$ and, with $\hat r:=\omega$,
$$\mathbf j\cdot\hat r=\frac{\hbar k}{m}\frac{|f(\omega)|^{2}}{r^{2}},\qquad \text{equivalently}\qquad r^{2}\,\mathbf j\cdot\hat r=\frac{\hbar k}{m}|f(\omega)|^{2},$$
and the current identity holds for every declared $f\in C^{1}(S^{2})$, with no
equation required of the field.

The assertion is an identity for the declared differentiable functions; it
constructs no probability law, no state, no beam and no cross section. The
fields of clause (c) are only $C^{1}$: an $f\in C^{1}(S^{2})$ need not admit
two angular derivatives, and no outgoing field is claimed here to solve the
free equation or to be stationary.

items.title: The declared short-range scattering model: state space, potential classes, assigned energy observables, asymptotic vocabulary and units
items.statement:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, the identical-particle
and spin postulate P6, and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Fix a mass parameter
$m>0$ and a spin label $s=0$, so that the framework's one-particle model
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] reads its state space as
$H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with the pairing linear in the first
argument, its componentwise position family $Q_{1},Q_{2},Q_{3}$, its
componentwise momentum family $P_{1},P_{2},P_{3}$ and the action constant
$\hbar>0$; the spin-zero internal factor carries the trivial representation of
P6. Units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: position
is read in metres, momentum in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, energy and potential
energy in joules, and $\hbar$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Choose a reference length $L_*>0$ in metres and put
$$y=x/L_*,\qquad E_*:=\frac{\hbar^2}{2mL_*^2},\qquad T_*:=\hbar/E_*.$$
Here $y$ is dimensionless, $E_*$ is in joules and $T_*$ in seconds.
The unitary coordinate dilation from physical-coordinate $L^2_x$ to
$L^2_y$ is $(D_*f)(y)=L_*^{3/2}f(L_*y)$, with inverse
$(D_*^*g)(x)=L_*^{-3/2}g(x/L_*)$. Lebesgue dilation
([[thm-lebesgue-measure-under-dilations-and-reflections]]) gives its norm
identity, first for simple functions and then by nonnegative approximation.
This convention makes all coordinates and spectral shifts in the tail
criterion below dimensionless; physical stationary equations retain $x$.

**(b) The declared scattering model and its potential classes.** As an
additional model assumption of the pair, adopt the **short-range scattering
model**. Its declared state space is $H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ of
clause (a), with the position and momentum families of that clause. A
**declared short-range potential** of the model is a real-valued measurable
function $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ satisfying either

1. *(compact-support class)* $V$ is bounded, $\|V\|_{\infty}<\infty$, and
   $V=0$ almost everywhere outside some ball
   $B_{\mathrm{supp}}:=\{x:|x|\le R_{\mathrm{supp}}\}$ with
   $R_{\mathrm{supp}}<\infty$; or
2. *(resolvent-tail class)* $V=V_{2}+V_{\mathrm b}$ with real
   $V_{2}\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ and real bounded $V_{\mathrm b}$, and, with
   the dimensionless reduced potential
   $W_*(y):=V(L_*y)/E_*=W_{*,2}(y)+W_{*,\mathrm b}(y)$ and
   $A_{0,*}:=-\Delta_y^{\mathrm{weak}}$ on $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3_y)$,
   the function
$$h_*(r):=\bigl\|M_{W_*}(A_{0,*}-iI)^{-1}\mathbf 1_{\{|y|\ge r\}}\bigr\|,\qquad r\ge0,$$
   is finite for every dimensionless $r$ and belongs to $L^1([0,\infty),dr)$.
   Equivalently the physical-coordinate operator is
   $M_V(H^{\mathrm{free}}-iE_*I)^{-1}\mathbf1_{\{|x|\ge L_*r\}}$:
   conjugation by $D_*$ gives exactly the displayed operator. Thus physical
   cutoffs have radius $L_*r$, and integration in physical radius $R$ gives
   $\int_0^\infty h_*(R/L_*)\,dR=L_*\int_0^\infty h_*(r)\,dr$.
   The reference length is fixed as part of this unit convention.

The function $V$ is read as a potential energy in joules; the model asserts no
derivation of $V$ from P5 or from any force law, and an assignment of a
concrete target to $V$ is a tested identification in the sense of clause (iii)
of P7 carrying the corresponding uncertainty. The pure Coulomb potential
$V(x)=-\kappa/|x|$, $\kappa>0$, is **not** in either class: it is a declared
long-range model with its own definition and comparison construction
on this page.

**(c) Assigned energy observables.** Let $\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary
Plancherel transform of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b), $c:=2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}/m$, and let
$$H^{\mathrm{free}}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad D(H^{\mathrm{free}}):=\bigl\{f\in H_{0}:|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in H_{0}\bigr\}$$
be the free operator of that clause with $d=3$ and $b=0$; by
[[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] its domain is
the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]) and
$H^{\mathrm{free}}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f$ with $\Delta_{w}$ the
weak Laplacian ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]).
For equations in physical coordinates write $A_{0,x}:=-\Delta_x^{\mathrm{weak}}$
and $W_x(x):=2mV(x)/\hbar^2$, so
$H^{\mathrm{free}}=(\hbar^2/2m)A_{0,x}$. Both $A_{0,x}$ and $W_x$
have inverse-square-length units; this energy division alone is not a
spatial nondimensionalization. Stationary items may abbreviate $W_x$ as $W$
(or its central radial profile as $w$), keeping physical $k$ and $r$.
The dimensionless operators instead satisfy
$$D_*H^{\mathrm{free}}D_*^*=E_*A_{0,*},\qquad D_*HD_*^*=E_*(A_{0,*}+M_{W_*}),\qquad W_*(y)=L_*^2W_x(L_*y).$$
Indeed testing the weak derivative definition after $x=L_*y$ gives
$\partial_y^\alpha D_*f=L_*^{|\alpha|}D_*(\partial_x^\alpha f)$ for
$|\alpha|\le2$; applying the inverse dilation gives the converse, so $D_*$
maps the physical Sobolev domain onto the dimensionless one. Multiplication
transforms by direct substitution, proving both operator identities on their
exact domains. The subscript $w$ in $\Delta_w$ above denotes weak derivatives,
not a coordinate or a unit convention.
With $M_V$ the maximal multiplication operator, $D(M_V)=\{f\in L^2:Vf\in L^2\}$ (bounded and everywhere defined in the compact-support class), the **assigned energy observables** of the model with declared
potential $V$ are the free operator $H^{\mathrm{free}}$ and the interacting
operator
$$H:=H^{\mathrm{free}}+M_{V},\qquad D(H):=D(H^{\mathrm{free}}).$$
The declared energy unit is the joule. For the compact-support class,
clause (c) of the cited theorem makes $H$ self-adjoint on $D(H)$ and bounded
below by $-\|V\|_{\infty}$; for the resolvent-tail class, self-adjointness of
$H$ on the same domain is proved on this page and is not presupposed here. The
model adopts $(H^{\mathrm{free}},\mathrm J)$ and $(H,\mathrm J)$ as assigned
sharp observables in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), and
reads their flows by [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]
with $U_{\mathrm{free}}(t)=e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$ and
$U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$.

**(d) Short-range scattering vocabulary.** For a declared short-range
potential $V$ the model declares the **free asymptotic comparison** to be the
pair of strong limits
$$\Omega_{\pm}:=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar},$$
which are declared **wave operators** of the model when both limits exist, and
declares the **scattering operator** $S:=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ when both
exist and $\Omega_{\pm}$ are isometries. The model says that the pair is
**asymptotically complete** for this $V$ when the two ranges agree with the
subspace
$$H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H):=\{\psi\in H_{0}:\mu^{H}_{\psi}\ll\lambda\},$$
where $\mu^{H}_{\psi}(B):=\langle E_{H}(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ is the scalar
spectral measure of the projection valued measure $E_{H}$ of the self-adjoint
operator $H$, and with
$$H_{\mathrm c}(H):=H_{\mathrm{pp}}(H)^{\perp},\qquad H_{\mathrm{pp}}(H):=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{\psi\ne0:H\psi=\lambda\psi\ \text{for some }\lambda\in\mathbb R\};$$
here $H_{\mathrm{pp}}(H)$ is the closed linear span of the eigenvectors of $H$.
An **asymptotic free state** of a vector $\psi\in H_{0}$ is a vector
$\psi_{\mathrm{in}}$ such that
$\bigl\|e^{-itH/\hbar}\psi-e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\psi_{\mathrm{in}}\bigr\|\to0$
as $t\to-\infty$; the model reads this limit relation through the
wave-operator identity $\psi=\Omega_{-}\psi_{\mathrm{in}}$ only when the wave
operator exists. These
are declarations of the model under P4; they construct no preparation,
detector or measured count, and no definition of a cross section appears here.

**(e) Status and scope.** Clause (a) adopts P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and P7 and
fixes the pair's spin-zero one-particle data, mass, action constant and choice
hypotheses. Clause (b) further adopts the compact-support and resolvent-tail
potential classes as **additional pair-level model assumptions**; neither
class follows from those postulates or from the cited mathematical results.
Clause (c) declares the assigned energy operators and their common domain;
the cited mathematics establishes self-adjointness where stated, including
the resolvent-tail case proved on the A page. Clause (d) declares the
comparison and spectral vocabulary without asserting that the limits exist
or are complete. No identification of $m$, $\hbar$ or $V$ with measured data
is asserted. Existence of the limits, completeness of the ranges and every
cross section are separate results of the pair.

items.physical_scope: The declared short-range scattering model of the pair: the spin-zero massive one-particle state space, an assigned external real potential in one of two declared short-range classes (bounded compact support, or a square-integrable plus bounded decomposition whose shifted free resolvent tail is integrable), the free and interacting assigned energy observables with the Coulomb tail explicitly excluded from the short-range classes, the Born position law, and the wave-operator and asymptotic-completeness vocabulary of the pair. The model is an additional assumption of the pair with a prescribed, not derived, potential; the long-range Coulomb case is a separate declared model. No preparation, no apparatus, no detector and no measured quantity appears.

items.title: The declared stationary elastic beam model: incident plane wave, scattered wave, current readings and differential and total cross sections
items.statement:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), with the short-range
scattering model of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]]: mass $m>0$, spin zero,
state space $H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, a declared short-range
potential $V$, the free and interacting assigned energy observables
$H^{\mathrm{free}}$ and $H$, its reading of the flow by
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], and the units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Incident plane-wave reading and declared density scale.** As an
additional model assumption of the pair, adopt the **stationary elastic beam
model**. Fix a **wave number** $k>0$ in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, a **direction**
$d\in S^2$, and an **incident number-density scale** $n_{\mathrm{inc}}>0$ in
$\mathrm{m^{-3}}$. This scale is an explicitly declared model normalization;
no numerical sample density or measured beam value is supplied. Retain the
unit-amplitude, dimensionless incident shape
$$u_{\mathrm{inc}}(x):=e^{ikd\cdot x},$$
with energy reading $E:=\hbar^2k^2/(2m)$ in joules. The **physical incident
beam field** is $\Phi_{\mathrm{inc}}:=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\,u_{\mathrm{inc}}$,
with unit $\mathrm{m^{-3/2}}$ and constant model number density
$|\Phi_{\mathrm{inc}}|^2=n_{\mathrm{inc}}$. For a dimensionless unit-amplitude
shape $\psi$, write $\mathbf j^{\mathrm{unit}}[\psi]:=(\hbar/m)\operatorname{Im}(\overline\psi\nabla\psi)$ for the mathematical current of
[[lem-nrqm-scattering-three-dimensional-current-and-flux]]. Its incident
value is $(\hbar k/m)d$, with velocity unit $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The model's
**physical number-current density** is the current of
$\Phi=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\psi$,
$$\mathbf j[\Phi]:=\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}(\overline\Phi\nabla\Phi)=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\mathbf j^{\mathrm{unit}}[\psi].$$
Thus the **incident current density** and **incident flux density** through a
plane normal to $d$ are
$$\mathbf j_{\mathrm{inc}}=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\frac{\hbar k}{m}d,\qquad J_{\mathrm{inc}}:=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\frac{\hbar k}{m}>0,$$
both in $\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}$ as in
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)5. The mathematical
plane-wave current of the cited lemma remains the unit-shape computation;
the density factor supplies the declared physical beam normalization.

**(c) Scattered-wave reading and generalized stationary solution.** For a
declared short-range potential $V$ the model declares a **generalized
stationary solution** at energy $E$ and direction $d$ to be a function
$\Psi:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb C$ of class $C^{2}$ on the complement of
$\operatorname{supp}V$ that satisfies
$$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\Psi+V\Psi=E\Psi$$
pointwise there and has the **outgoing asymptotic reading**
$$\Psi(x)=e^{ikd\cdot x}+\frac{f_{k}(\Omega)}{r}e^{ikr}+\mathcal E(x),\qquad x=r\Omega,\ r\to\infty,$$
with a **scattering amplitude** function $f_k:S^2\to\mathbb C$, read in
metres relative to the unit incident shape, and a physical beam field
$\Phi:=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\Psi$ with unit $\mathrm{m^{-3/2}}$. The same
constant factor multiplies its incident, outgoing and remainder terms;
$f_k$ remains the amplitude relative to the incident field, in metres.
Here $\Omega:=x/r$ is the **outgoing unit direction**, and the precise decay
of the remainder $\mathcal E$ is fixed by the existence theorem of this page.
The **scattered physical field** is
$\Phi_{\mathrm{sc}}:=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}(\Psi-u_{\mathrm{inc}})$.
The physical scattered radial current density, obtained by applying the
quadratic current formula to this scattered component, is
$$j_r^{\mathrm{sc}}(r,\Omega)=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\left(\frac{\hbar k}{m}\frac{|f_k(\Omega)|^2}{r^2}+O(r^{-3})\right)\qquad(r\to\infty),$$
in $\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}$ for the fixed declared density scale. The leading
unit-shape current is clause (c) of
[[lem-nrqm-scattering-three-dimensional-current-and-flux]]; the current of
the remainder is controlled by the stationary theorem. The definition uses
the scattered component, with no assumption that incident/scattered
interference in the total field vanishes.
A generalized stationary solution is generally not an element of $H_{0}$; it
is not a preparation of the model, and clause (d) of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] does not apply to it. It
is used only through the declared flux quantities computed from it, and every
such use states the idealization.

**(d) Differential and total cross-section readings.** Under the declared
**equal-channel elastic flux assumptions** -- that the incident and outgoing
readings refer to the same elastic channel at the same energy, that the
incident flux density is spatially uniform over the transverse extent of the
target and the outgoing current is read far outside the support of $V$ -- the
model declares the **differential cross section**
$$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(\Omega):=\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{r^{2}\,j^{\mathrm{sc}}_{r}(r,\Omega)}{J_{\mathrm{inc}}} =|f_{k}(\Omega)|^{2},$$
read in $\mathrm{m^{2}\,sr^{-1}}$, and the **total cross section**
$$\sigma:=\int_{S^{2}}\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(\Omega)\,d\Omega =\int_{S^{2}}|f_{k}(\Omega)|^{2}\,d\Omega,$$
read in $\mathrm{m^{2}}$, whenever the displayed limit and integral exist; the
existence and finiteness of both are proved on this page for the declared
classes. The common positive density factor cancels in the ratio,
$r^2j_r^{\mathrm{sc}}/J_{\mathrm{inc}}\to |f_k|^2$, so the cross sections are
independent of the declared $n_{\mathrm{inc}}$. This normalization supplies
no relation to the energy outcome law of P2 and no assertion that an $L^2$
preparation realizes either stationary field.

**(e) Status and scope.** Clauses (b)-(d) are declarations of the pair under
P1, P2, P4 and P7 together with the short-range model; they are an idealized
stationary reading and not a model of an apparatus. The new density scale is
a symbolic normalization parameter of that reading, not a measured sample
value; multiplication by $\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}$ does not turn the
stationary shape into an $L^2$ preparation. In particular no beam
source, target density, collimation, detector acceptance, efficiency,
background or counting procedure appears, and the symbols
$d\sigma/d\Omega$ and $\sigma$ denote model quantities computed from the
declared solution. An identification of a measured count cross section with
these quantities requires a separate preparation and detection model and
carries the uncertainty of that identification.

items.title: Existence of the model's wave operators, isometry and intertwining, and the purely absolutely continuous free spectrum
items.statement:
Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass parameter $m>0$,
spin zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and a declared potential $V$ of the
**compact-support class**, so that $V$ is real, bounded and vanishes almost
everywhere outside a ball $B_{R}$; let $H^{\mathrm{free}}$ and
$H=H^{\mathrm{free}}+M_{V}$ be the assigned energy observables of the model on
$D(H)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, and let $\Omega_{\pm}$, $S$,
$\mu^{H}_{\psi}$ and $H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)$ be as in clause (d) of that
definition. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $H$ is self-adjoint on $D(H)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and bounded
below, and for every Schwartz function $\psi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]])
$$\int_{0}^{\infty}\bigl\|Ve^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\psi\bigr\|_{2}\,dt<\infty, \qquad \int_{-\infty}^{0}\bigl\|Ve^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\psi\bigr\|_{2}\,dt<\infty;$$

(b) the strong limits
$$\Omega_{\pm}=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$$
exist as bounded linear isometries of $H_{0}$, so $\Omega_{\pm}^{*}\Omega_{\pm}=I$;
they intertwine the two flows,
$$e^{-isH/\hbar}\Omega_{\pm}=\Omega_{\pm}e^{-isH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\qquad(s\in\mathbb R),$$
and satisfy $H\Omega_{\pm}\psi=\Omega_{\pm}H^{\mathrm{free}}\psi$ for every
$\psi\in D(H^{\mathrm{free}})$;

(c) the free operator has purely absolutely continuous spectrum: for every
$\psi\in H_{0}$ the scalar measure $\mu^{H^{\mathrm{free}}}_{\psi}$ is
absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure and gives zero mass to
$\{0\}$ and to $(-\infty,0)$; hence
$H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H^{\mathrm{free}})=H_{\mathrm c}(H^{\mathrm{free}})=H_{0}$
and $H^{\mathrm{free}}$ has no eigenvalues;

(d) $H$ has no eigenvalue in $(0,\infty)$: if $\psi\in D(H)$, $\psi\ne0$ and
$H\psi=\lambda\psi$ with $\lambda>0$, then no such $\psi$ exists.

The statement is conditional on the declared model and the cited mathematics.
It asserts no completeness of the ranges, no unitarity of $S$, no cross
section and no measured quantity; completeness is the content of the two
following theorems of this page.

items.title: Asymptotic completeness and the unitary scattering operator for real bounded compactly supported potentials
items.statement:
Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$ and a declared **compact-support-class**
potential $V$ supported in a ball $B_{R}$. Let $\Omega_{\pm}$ and $S$ be the
wave operators and scattering operator of clause (d) of that definition,
$E_{H}$ the projection valued measure of the self-adjoint interacting operator
$H$, and $\mu^{H}_{\psi}$ its scalar measures. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) the wave operators exist by
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-wave-operator-existence-and-free-continuity]], and
$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{\pm}\subseteq H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)$ and
$H_{\mathrm{sc}}(H)=\{0\}$, where
$$H_{\mathrm{sc}}(H):=\{\psi\in H_{0}:\mu^{H}_{\psi}\ \text{is atomless and singular with respect to Lebesgue measure}\};$$

(b) each wave operator is asymptotically complete,
$$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{+}=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{-}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)=H_{\mathrm c}(H);$$

(c) $S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ is unitary on $H_{0}$ and commutes with the
free flow, $Se^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}=e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}S$ for
every $t\in\mathbb R$.

The statement is a conditional consequence of the declared model with a
compactly supported real bounded potential; it asserts no stationary amplitude,
no partial-wave decomposition, no cross section and no measured quantity.

items.title: Asymptotic completeness for the resolvent-tail short-range class, with the decaying-tail example and the explicit exclusion of the Coulomb tail
items.statement:
Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and a declared potential $V$ of the
**resolvent-tail class**: real $V=V_{2}+V_{\mathrm b}$ with
$V_{2}\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ and $V_{\mathrm b}\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{3})$
real, and, with the model's reference length $L_*$, energy $E_*=\hbar^2/(2mL_*^2)$, dimensionless coordinate $y=x/L_*$, reduced potential $W_*(y)=V(L_*y)/E_*$ and the
nondimensional free operator $A_{0,*}:=-\Delta_y^{\mathrm{weak}}$ of the model,
$$h_*(r):=\bigl\|M_{W_*}(A_{0,*}-iI)^{-1}\mathbf 1_{\{|y|\ge r\}}\bigr\|,$$
finite for every dimensionless $r\ge0$ and in $L^{1}([0,\infty))$.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $H=H^{\mathrm{free}}+M_{V}$ is self-adjoint on
$D(H)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]); both wave operators
$$\Omega_{\pm}=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$$
exist as bounded linear isometries, $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{+}=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{-}
=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)=H_{\mathrm c}(H)$, and $H_{\mathrm{sc}}(H)=\{0\}$;

(b) $S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ is unitary on $H_{0}$;

(c) the conclusions of (a) and (b) hold in particular for a declared potential
of the explicit **decaying-tail form** $V=V_{\mathrm{loc}}+V_{\mathrm{tail}}$
with real $V_{\mathrm{loc}}\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ compactly supported and
$|V_{\mathrm{tail}}(x)|\le C(1+|x|/L_*)^{-1-\delta}$ almost everywhere for some
constants $C>0$ in joules and dimensionless $\delta>0$; here the integrability hypothesis of the preamble
is not presupposed, because the cited theorem supplies it for this form;

(d) the explicit decaying-tail form of (c) does not cover the pure Coulomb
potential $V(x)=-\kappa/|x|$, $\kappa>0$: after any split into a compactly
supported $L^{2}$ part and a tail part, the bound
$|V_{\mathrm{tail}}(x)|\le C(1+|x|/L_*)^{-1-\delta}$ fails for every $\delta>0$,
because $\kappa(1+|x|/L_*)^{1+\delta}/|x|\to+\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$. The pure Coulomb potential also fails the general resolvent-tail integrability hypothesis itself, as proved below; the Coulomb case is the separate
declared long-range model of this page.

The statement is conditional on the declared model with the displayed
integrability hypothesis and the cited mathematics; no cross section,
stationary amplitude or measured quantity is asserted.

items.title: The model's stationary scattering wave, its outgoing amplitude and the differential and total cross-section readings
items.statement:
Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and action constant $\hbar>0$, with a **compact-support-class** potential
$V$ supported in the ball $B_{R}$, and adopt the declared stationary elastic
beam model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]] at wave number
$k>0$, direction $d\in S^2$ and the declared $n_{\mathrm{inc}}>0$ in
$\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, with incident energy $E=\hbar^2k^2/(2m)$.
The construction below retains the dimensionless unit-incident shape
$\Psi$; its physical beam field is $\Phi=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\Psi$.
Put
$$W:=\frac{2m}{\hbar^{2}}V,\qquad G_{k}(z):=\frac{e^{ik|z|}}{4\pi|z|},\qquad (K_{k}f)(x):=\int_{B_{R}}G_{k}(x-y)W(y)f(y)\,dy$$
for $f\in L^{2}(B_{R};\mathbb C)$ and $x\in B_{R}$. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $I+K_{k}$ is boundedly invertible on $L^{2}(B_{R};\mathbb C)$; with
$u:=(I+K_{k})^{-1}\bigl(e^{ikd\cdot x}|_{B_{R}}\bigr)$ and
$$\Psi(x):=e^{ikd\cdot x}-\int_{B_{R}}G_{k}(x-y)W(y)u(y)\,dy,$$
one has $\Psi\in H^{2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^{3})$,
$(-\Delta+W-k^{2})\Psi=0$ distributionally on $\mathbb R^{3}$, and
$\Psi|_{B_{R}}=u$;

(b) with $r=|x|>2R$ and $\Omega=x/r$, the **scattering amplitude**
$$f_{k}(\Omega):=-\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{B_{R}}e^{-ik\Omega\cdot y}W(y)u(y)\,dy$$
is smooth on $S^{2}$ and
$$\Psi(x)=e^{ikd\cdot x}+\frac{e^{ikr}f_{k}(\Omega)}{r}+\mathcal E(x),$$
where $|\mathcal E(x)|+|\partial_{r}\mathcal E(x)|\le C(k,R,\|Wu\|_{1})r^{-2}$
uniformly in $\Omega$, and for every fixed product $D_{\Omega}$ of smooth
tangential differential operators on $S^{2}$ also
$|D_{\Omega}\mathcal E|+|D_{\Omega}\partial_{r}\mathcal E|\le C_{D}r^{-2}$;

(c) the physical scattered radial current of the beam model, with
$\Phi_{\mathrm{sc}}=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}(\Psi-e^{ikd\cdot x})$, is
$$j_r^{\mathrm{sc}}(r,\Omega)=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\left(\frac{\hbar k}{m}\frac{|f_k(\Omega)|^2}{r^2}+O(r^{-3})\right)$$
uniformly in $\Omega$, with physical incident flux density
$J_{\mathrm{inc}}=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\hbar k/m$ in $\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}$;
the common density factor cancels, and the cross-section readings are
$$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(\Omega)=|f_{k}(\Omega)|^{2}\qquad\text{in }\mathrm{m^{2}\,sr^{-1}}, \qquad \sigma=\int_{S^{2}}|f_{k}(\Omega)|^{2}\,d\Omega<\infty\qquad\text{in }\mathrm{m^{2}};$$

(d) the solution $\Psi$ of (a) is a generalized stationary solution of the
beam model at energy $E$ and direction $d$ in the sense of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]], and no other
function satisfying the same equation on the complement of
$\operatorname{supp}V$ and the same outgoing reading is produced by the
construction.

Every assertion is conditional on the declared model and the cited
mathematics. The stationary wave is not an element of the state space; the
item asserts no preparation, no beam apparatus, no detector acceptance and no
measured count rate.

items.title: The model's partial-wave and phase-shift vocabulary for a declared central potential
items.statement:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and its stationary elastic beam model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]] at wave
number $k>0$; adopt the declared central-potential reading of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-central-potential-model]]: a **declared central
potential** of the pair is a real bounded measurable $V(x)=v(|x|)$ with
$v:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ bounded, and it is **short-range** when it lies in
the compact-support class of the scattering model. Units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the wave number $k$ is read in
$\mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and the energy $E=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)$ in joules.

**(b) Channel vocabulary.** For a declared central short-range potential $V$
and a channel label $(l,m)$ with $l\ge0$ and $-l\le m\le l$, the model
declares the **partial wave** $l$ and reads the angular dependence in the
complete spherical harmonic family $(Y_{lm})$ of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-partial-wave-cross-section-convergence]]; the
labels $l,m$ are indices of that family. The reduced equation below is read in
physical coordinates after energy division: the reduced potential is
$w:=2mv/\hbar^{2}$ of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] and the energy-divided spectral value is $k^{2}$, both in $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$,
so that the physical parameters $m,\hbar$ do not enter it explicitly. The
model declares the **regular radial solution**
$\varphi_{l}$ of the reduced equation
$$-\varphi_{l}''+\Bigl(w(r)+\frac{l(l+1)}{r^{2}}\Bigr)\varphi_{l}=k^{2}\varphi_{l}, \qquad \varphi_{l}(r)/r^{l+1}\longrightarrow1\quad(r\to0),$$
and the **outgoing radial solution** $f_{l}$ with
$$f_{l}(r)=e^{i(kr-l\pi/2)}\bigl(1+O(r^{-1})\bigr)\qquad(r\to\infty)$$
outside the interaction region; these are the functions constructed by the
cited theorem, and they are not asserted to be elements of the state space.

**(c) Channel factor and phase shift.** The model declares the **channel
factor** and the **phase shift** of the partial wave $l$ to be
$$S_{l}(k):=\frac{\overline{W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})}}{W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})}, \qquad S_{l}(k)=e^{2i\delta_{l}(k)},$$
where $W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})=\varphi_{l}f_{l}'-\varphi_{l}'f_{l}$ is the
Wronskian and $\delta_{l}(k)$ is the **phase shift**, a real number read
modulo $\pi$; the model reads $|S_{l}(k)|=1$ and calls the channel
**elastic**. The declared **channel cross-section reading** is
$$\sigma_{l}(k):=\frac{4\pi}{k^{2}}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}(k),$$
read in $\mathrm{m^{2}}$. The existence of the functions and the identities
$|S_{l}|=1$ and $\sum_{l}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}<\infty$ are proved on this
page and are not presupposed here.

**(d) Status and scope.** Clauses (b)-(c) are declarations of the pair: names
for the objects constructed by the cited mathematics and the reading of the
phase shift modulo $\pi$. The model asserts no identification of the labels
$l,m$ with a measured angular momentum of a material system, no statement
about bound states or their count, and no channel decomposition for
non-central potentials. Every numerical statement about $\delta_{l}$ is a
separate theorem or example of the pair.

The definition is a reading of the stationary model of the pair; it asserts no angular-momentum interpretation of the labels for a material system, no bound-state statement and no measured quantity.

items.title: The declared single-channel resonance model: pole-shaped channel factor and its cross-section reading
items.statement:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and action constant $\hbar>0$, and its partial-wave and phase-shift
reading [[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] for a
declared central short-range potential. Fix a **channel label** $l\in\{0,1,2,\dots\}$
in the sense of clause (b) of that reading. Units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**(b) The declared single-channel resonance model.** As an additional model
assumption of the pair, fix real **resonance parameters** $E_{r}$ and
$\Gamma>0$, both read in joules, and **declare** the channel factor of the
label $l$ to be
$$S_{l}(E):=\frac{E-E_{r}-i\Gamma/2}{E-E_{r}+i\Gamma/2}\qquad(E>0),$$
read for positive energies only, with the **phase shift** of the channel read
from the relation $S_{l}=e^{2i\delta_{l}}$ modulo $\pi$ and the **channel
cross-section reading**
$$\sigma_{l}(E):=\frac{4\pi}{k(E)^{2}}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}(E), \qquad k(E):=\frac{\sqrt{2mE}}{\hbar},$$
read in $\mathrm{m^{2}}$. The model calls $E_{r}$ the **resonance energy** and
$\Gamma$ the **width parameter**; both are declared model parameters and
neither is identified with a measured quantity. The parameter $E_r$ may be
zero or negative; calling it a resonance energy does not assign a physical
cross section at that parameter value unless $E_r>0$. Auxiliary real-axis
algebraic comparisons of the Lorentzian factor do not extend $k(E)$ or
$\sigma_l(E)$ beyond the positive-energy domain.

**(c) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(b) declare a conditional one-channel
model. The pair asserts no analytic continuation, no pole of the resolvent and
no property of any potential that would produce the declared factor
$S_{l}$; the model is used only to compute the induced phase shift and channel
cross section of the declared factor. In particular, no exponential decay law,
no lifetime $\hbar/\Gamma$ and no Lorentzian line shape of a measured
distribution is asserted or derived; those would be separate models with their
own assumptions and their own uncertainty qualifications.

The model is a declared conditional model of one channel; it makes no assertion that a potential produces this factor, claims no decay law or lifetime identification, and asserts no measured line width or count.

items.title: Partial-wave expansion, unit-modulus channel factors and the phase-shift cross-section series
items.statement:
Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and a **declared central short-range potential** $V(x)=v(|x|)$ in the
sense of [[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]]
clause (a): $v$ is real, bounded and $V$ is supported in a ball $B_{R}$. Adopt
the stationary elastic beam model at wave number $k>0$ and direction
$d\in S^{2}$, with amplitude $f_{k}$ as in
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]], and the
channel vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] clauses (b),
(c). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $f_{k}$ depends only on $\cos\theta=\Omega\cdot d$, and its **Legendre
expansion**
$$f_{k}(\theta)=\frac{1}{2ik}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)\bigl(S_{l}(k)-1\bigr)P_{l}(\cos\theta)$$
converges in $L^{2}(S^{2})$ and absolutely, so the model's cross-section
reading is
$$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(\theta)=|f_{k}(\theta)|^{2};$$

(b) the channel factors are unit modulus, $|S_{l}(k)|=1$, the phase shifts
$\delta_{l}(k)$ are real modulo $\pi$, and the **total cross section** of the
beam model is
$$\sigma=\frac{\pi}{k^{2}}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)|S_{l}(k)-1|^{2} =\frac{4\pi}{k^{2}}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}(k)\qquad\text{in }\mathrm{m^{2}},$$
the series converging, with the channel readings of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] clause (c) as
its summands;

(c) the objects $\varphi_{l}$, $f_{l}$, $S_{l}$ and $\delta_{l}$ of the
channel vocabulary are exactly the regular and outgoing radial solutions, the
Wronskian ratio and the phase shift constructed by the cited mathematics for
the reduced radial potential $w=(2m/\hbar^2)v$ at the model's wave number $k$; the phase shifts
are not asserted to have a definite sign and no low-energy limit is asserted
beyond the convergence of the series.

The statement is conditional on the declared central model, the beam model
and the cited mathematics; it asserts no measured angular distribution and no
identification of $l$ with a measured angular momentum.

items.title: The controlled Born reading: operator-norm condition, uniform amplitude error and coupling scaling
items.statement:
Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and a **compact-support-class** potential $V$ supported in $B_{R}$, adopt
the stationary elastic beam model at wave number $k>0$ and direction
$d\in S^{2}$, and let
$$W:=\frac{2m}{\hbar^{2}}V,\qquad G_{k}(z)=\frac{e^{ik|z|}}{4\pi|z|},\qquad (K_{k}f)(x)=\int_{B_{R}}G_{k}(x-y)W(y)f(y)\,dy$$
and $u=(I+K_{k})^{-1}e_{\mathrm{inc}}$, $f_{k}$ be as in
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]], with
$e_{\mathrm{inc}}=e^{ikd\cdot x}|_{B_{R}}$. Put $q:=\|K_{k}\|$, the operator
norm of [[def-operator-norm]] and [[def-bounded-linear-operator]], and
$$f_{B}(\Omega):=-\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{B_{R}}e^{ik(d-\Omega)\cdot y}W(y)\,dy$$
for $\Omega\in S^{2}$, read in metres. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
Then:

(a) the operator $K_{k}$ is bounded, $q<\infty$, and if $q<1$ the exact
stationary solution satisfies
$$\bigl\|u-e_{\mathrm{inc}}\bigr\|_{L^{2}(B_{R})}\le\frac{q}{1-q}\, \bigl\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\bigr\|_{L^{2}(B_{R})};$$

(b) under the same condition $q<1$ the **Born amplitude** $f_{B}$ approximates
the exact amplitude uniformly,
$$\bigl|f_{k}(\Omega)-f_{B}(\Omega)\bigr|\le \frac{\|W\|_{\infty}\,|B_{R}|^{1/2}}{4\pi}\,\frac{q}{1-q}\, \bigl\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\bigr\|_{L^{2}(B_{R})} \qquad(\Omega\in S^{2}),$$
with $|B_{R}|=4\pi R^{3}/3$;

(c) *coupling scaling.* For a real or complex multiplier $\eta$ with
$|\eta|q<1$, let $u_{\eta}:=(I+\eta K_{k})^{-1}e_{\mathrm{inc}}$, let
$f_{k,\eta}(\Omega;d):=-\eta(4\pi)^{-1}\int_{B_R}e^{-ik\Omega\cdot y}W(y)u_\eta(y;d)\,dy$ be the amplitude for the scaled potential $\eta W$, and let $f_{B}$ be as above. Then
$$\bigl\|u_{\eta}-e_{\mathrm{inc}}\bigr\|_{2}\le\frac{|\eta|q}{1-|\eta|q} \bigl\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\bigr\|_{2},\qquad \sup_{\Omega,d\in S^{2}}\bigl|f_{k,\eta}(\Omega;d)-\eta f_{B}(\Omega;d)\bigr| \le\frac{|\eta|^{2}\|W\|_{\infty}|B_{R}|q}{4\pi(1-|\eta|q)};$$
in particular no condition on the base operator norm of $K_{k}$ itself is
needed for (c).

The statement is conditional on the declared model and the cited mathematics;
the condition $q<1$ is an operator-norm condition on the declared potential,
kernel and wave number, not a vague smallness of $V$, and no measured cross
section is asserted.

items.title: Identification of the model's scattering operator with the on-shell stationary operator, and the central per-channel form
items.statement:
Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and a **compact-support-class** potential $V$ supported in $B_{R}$; by
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-compact-support-asymptotic-completeness]] the model's
wave operators exist and
$$S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$$
is unitary on $H_{0}$ and commutes with the free flow. Write $\sigma$ for
surface measure on $S^{2}$ and $\mathfrak h=L^{2}(S^{2},d\sigma)$, and for
every $d\in S^{2}$ let $f_{k}(\cdot,d)$ be the model's stationary amplitude
of [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]] at incident
direction $d$, with the operator $\mathcal A_{k}$ on $\mathfrak h$ defined by
$$(\mathcal A_{k}a)(\Omega):=\int_{S^{2}}f_{k}(\Omega,d)\,a(d)\,d\sigma(d).$$
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) the free flow is diagonalized by the free trace transform of the cited
mathematics, a unitary $F_{0}:H_{0}\to L^{2}((0,\infty),dE;\mathfrak h)$ with
$(F_{0}g)(E,\omega)=E^{1/4}2^{-1/2}\widehat g(\sqrt E\,\omega)$ in the
energy-divided variables of the scaling correspondence, where this auxiliary $E=k^2$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$ and the physical energy is $(\hbar^2/2m)E$, and the model's
scattering operator is carried into multiplication,
$$F_{0}\,S\,F_{0}^{*}=M_{S(E)};$$

(b) for almost every $E=k^{2}>0$ the on-shell operator is
$$S(E)=I+\frac{ik}{2\pi}\mathcal A_{k},$$
a unitary operator on $\mathfrak h$, and the model's stationary amplitude
$f_{k}(\Omega,d)$ is the kernel of $\mathcal A_{k}$;

(c) for $R\in SO(3)$ let $V_{R}(x):=V(R^{-1}x)$ and $(U_{R}a)(\omega):=a(R^{-1}\omega)$;
then
$$S[V_{R}](E)=U_{R}\,S[V](E)\,U_{R}^{-1};$$

(d) if $V$ is in addition central, the fiber decomposes in the spherical
harmonic basis as $S(E)Y_{lm}=S_{l}(k)Y_{lm}$, where $S_{l}$ and
$\delta_{l}$ are the model's channel factor and phase shift of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]], equal to the
Wronskian ratio $\overline{W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})}/W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})$, and
the cross-section reading of
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-cross-section]] is the phase-shift series
of that channel decomposition.

The statement identifies operators and operators-valued functions of the
declared model; it asserts no measurement of $S$ or $S(E)$, no detector model
and no empirical claim.

items.title: The declared long-range Coulomb model and its Dollard-modified free comparison
items.statement:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), with the spin-zero
state space $H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, mass $m>0$, action
constant $\hbar>0$ and the units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) The declared Coulomb model.** As an additional model assumption of the
pair, fix a **coupling** $\kappa>0$, read in $\mathrm{J\,m}$, and adopt the
**one-centre Coulomb model** of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] in its spin-zero
one-particle reading: the declared potential is
$$V_{\kappa}(x):=-\frac{\kappa}{|x|}\qquad(x\ne0),$$
read in joules, with the value at the origin a declared convention that does
not affect the theory, and the **assigned energy observable** is
$$H_{\kappa}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}-\frac{\kappa}{|\cdot|}$$
on the domain $H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$,
self-adjoint there by
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]] clause (a) with flow
$e^{-itH_{\kappa}/\hbar}$ in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]. The model declares the
free comparison operator to be the free assigned energy observable
$H^{\mathrm{free}}$ of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clause (c), and reads its
Coulomb coupling in the inverse-length form
$$\gamma:=\frac{2m\kappa}{\hbar^{2}}\quad(\mathrm{m^{-1}}), \qquad\text{so that}\qquad H_{\kappa}=c\Bigl(-\Delta_{w}-\frac{\gamma}{|\cdot|}\Bigr),\quad c=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}.$$
The pure Coulomb potential is **not** in the short-range classes of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clause (b); it is the
model's long-range case.

**(c) The declared Dollard-modified comparison.** Choose a reference length $\ell_\star>0$, read in metres, as a comparison convention, and put
$$t_{\star}:=\frac{2m\ell_\star^2}{\hbar}\quad(\mathrm{s}).$$
and, for $t\ne0$, let $h_{t}:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb C$ be the bounded Borel
function
$$h_{t}(x):=\exp\Bigl(i\,\operatorname{sign}(t)\, \frac{m\kappa}{\hbar\sqrt{2mx}}\,\log\frac{|t|}{t_{\star}}\Bigr)\quad(x>0), \qquad h_{t}(0):=1 .$$
The model declares the **Dollard-modified free comparison** to be the family
$$U_{D}(t):=e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\,h_{t}(H^{\mathrm{free}})\quad(t\ne0), \qquad U_{D}(0):=I,$$
where $h_{t}(H^{\mathrm{free}})$ is the bounded functional calculus
([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]] clause 1) of the self-adjoint free
operator: since $h_{t}$ is unimodular, $U_{D}(t)$ is unitary for every $t$,
and both factors are functions of $H^{\mathrm{free}}$ and commute. The
**modified wave operators** of the model are the strong limits
$$\Omega_{D\pm}:=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH_{\kappa}/\hbar}U_{D}(t),$$
declared when both exist, and the **modified scattering operator** is
$S_{D}:=\Omega_{D+}^{*}\Omega_{D-}$ when both exist and are isometries. The
reference length and the resulting time $t_\star$ are declared conventions. More exactly, changing the reference time from $t_\star$ to $t_\star'$ multiplies $U_D(t)$ on the right, for each sign $\sigma=\operatorname{sign}t$, by the fixed free-energy unitary
$$Q_\sigma= q_\sigma(H^{\mathrm{free}}),\qquad q_\sigma(E)=\exp\Bigl(-i\sigma\frac{m\kappa}{\hbar\sqrt{2mE}}\log\frac{t_\star'}{t_\star}\Bigr)\quad(E>0),\qquad q_\sigma(0)=1.$$
It is a bounded unimodular Borel multiplier and commutes with the free flow. Hence, when the wave operators exist, $\Omega_{D\pm}'=\Omega_{D\pm}Q_\pm$ and $S_D'=Q_+^*S_DQ_-$. The completeness and isometry properties are unchanged; these are the fixed outgoing and incoming phase conventions.

**(d) Status and scope.** Clauses (b)-(c) are declarations of the pair: a
prescribed long-range potential with its assigned energy observable, and a
modified comparison construction for it. The model asserts no formula for a
Coulomb scattering amplitude, no Rutherford cross section and no measured
quantity; the modification is a comparison construction for the long-range
generator, not a new interaction or a measured force. The ordinary
short-range comparison of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clause (d) is not claimed
to be complete for the Coulomb model; its completeness is established only
for the modified comparison, on this page.

R. Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Section 15.4 printed pages 214-215: the Yukawa potential reducing to the Coulomb potential as the screening length increases, and Rutherford scattering

The model is an additional assumption of the pair; the reference time is a declared convention that changes only asymptotic channel phases, and the definition asserts no Rutherford amplitude, no measured cross section and no identification of kappa with measured charge data.

items.title: Completeness of the Dollard-modified wave operators for the declared Coulomb model
items.statement:
Adopt the declared long-range Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-coulomb-dollard-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin zero,
action constant $\hbar>0$, coupling $\kappa>0$, the assigned energy operator
$H_{\kappa}$ on $H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the free operator
$H^{\mathrm{free}}$, the inverse-length coupling
$\gamma=2m\kappa/\hbar^{2}$, a declared reference length $\ell_\star>0$ in metres and reference time $t_{\star}=2m\ell_\star^2/\hbar$, the
Dollard-modified comparison $U_{D}(t)$ and the modified wave operators
$\Omega_{D\pm}$ and $S_{D}$ of that definition. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) the modified wave operators exist as strong limits and are bounded linear
isometries, $\Omega_{D\pm}^{*}\Omega_{D\pm}=I$, and they intertwine,
$$\Omega_{D\pm}e^{-isH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}=e^{-isH_{\kappa}/\hbar}\Omega_{D\pm} \qquad(s\in\mathbb R);$$

(b) the modified wave operators are complete,
$$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D+}=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D-} =H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_{\kappa})=H_{\mathrm c}(H_{\kappa});$$

(c) the modified scattering operator $S_{D}=\Omega_{D+}^{*}\Omega_{D-}$ is
unitary on $H_{0}$ and commutes with the free flow;

(d) the ordinary short-range comparison of the model is not substituted:
neither existence nor completeness of
$\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH_{\kappa}/\hbar}e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$
is asserted, and the modification is essential to the statement.

The statement is conditional on the declared model and the cited
mathematics. It asserts no explicit Coulomb scattering amplitude, no
Rutherford or other cross section, and no measured quantity; the logarithmic
phase is a comparison construction for the long-range generator.

items.physical_scope: The declared long-range Coulomb model with coupling kappa>0 and its Dollard-modified free comparison: existence of the modified wave operators as strong limits, their isometry and intertwining, the completeness equalities of their ranges with the absolutely continuous and continuous subspaces of the Coulomb operator, and unitarity of the modified scattering operator. Conditional on the declared model and the cited mathematics; the item asserts no Coulomb scattering amplitude, no Rutherford cross section, no measured quantity and no ordinary short-range comparison for the Coulomb potential.

items.title: The resonance model's phase-shift law, unitarity and channel cross section
items.statement:
Adopt the declared single-channel resonance model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-model]] with channel label $l$,
mass $m>0$, action constant $\hbar>0$ and parameters $E_{r}\in\mathbb R$,
$\Gamma>0$, with the phase shift read modulo $\pi$ from $S_{l}=e^{2i\delta_{l}}$
and the channel cross-section reading $\sigma_{l}(E)$ of that definition.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Put $y:=\Gamma/2>0$.
For every real $E$ define the **auxiliary real-axis Lorentzian factor**
$$L(E):=\frac{y^2}{(E-E_r)^2+y^2}.$$
This is a mathematical extension of the positive-energy phase-shift factor;
physical phase shifts, $k(E)$ and cross sections remain defined only for $E>0$.
Then:

(a) for every $E>0$, $|S_l(E)|=1$ and
$$\delta_l(E)=-\operatorname{Arg}(E-E_r+iy)\quad(\mathrm{modulo}\ \pi),$$
where for $z=x+iy$ with $y>0$, $\operatorname{Arg}z$ is the unique angle
$\theta\in(0,\pi)$ with $\cos\theta=x/\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$ and
$\sin\theta=y/\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$. Equivalently, for $E\ne E_r$ one may use
$\delta_l(E)=-\arctan(y/(E-E_r))$ modulo $\pi$; if $E=E_r>0$,
$\delta_l(E)=-\pi/2$ modulo $\pi$;

(b) for every $E>0$, $\sin^2\delta_l(E)=L(E)$. On the entire real axis,
$L(E)$ has value $1$ exactly at $E=E_r$ and value $1/2$ exactly at
$E=E_r\pm\Gamma/2$. Thus the **full-real-axis half-height width** of this
factor is $\Gamma$ for every real $E_r$. A peak or half-height location is
in the physical energy range only when that location is positive; the
width statement itself concerns $L$ on $\mathbb R$;

(c) for every $E>0$, the channel cross-section reading is
$$\sigma_l(E)=\frac{4\pi}{k(E)^2}(2l+1)L(E),\qquad k(E)=\frac{\sqrt{2mE}}{\hbar},$$
read in $\mathrm{m^2}$. If $E_r>0$, its value at that physical energy is
$$\sigma_l(E_r)=\frac{4\pi\hbar^2}{2mE_r}(2l+1).$$
If $E_r\le0$, this model defines no physical cross section at $E_r$.
No maximum statement at $E_r$ is made for $\sigma_l$ itself, whose energy
dependence also contains the factor $k(E)^{-2}$; no slow-variation
assumption on that factor is required.

Every display is a conditional algebraic statement about the declared model;
no potential producing $S_{l}$, no decay law, no lifetime and no measured
quantity is asserted.

R. Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Section 15.7 printed pages 219-221: low-energy scattering and the scattering length

Half-height locations have a physical reading only when positive. Conditional algebra of a declared model; no producing potential, decay law, lifetime or measured width or count is asserted.

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the three-dimensional scattering page
items.statement:
## Remarks

**What the page establishes, and what it does not.**

- *Model deductions.* The page proves, conditionally on the declared
  short-range model and the cited mathematics, the existence of the wave
  operators, their isometry and intertwining
  ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-wave-operator-existence-and-free-continuity]]), the
  asymptotic completeness and unitarity of the scattering operator for the
  compact-support and resolvent-tail classes
  ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-compact-support-asymptotic-completeness]],
  [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-resolvent-tail-asymptotic-completeness]]), the
  stationary outgoing solution with its amplitude and the cross-section
  readings ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]]), the controlled
  Born approximation with its operator-norm condition
  ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-controlled-born-approximation]]), the phase-shift
  cross-section series, the on-shell operator identification, and the
  conditional resonance-model algebra. Every one of these is a logical
  consequence of the stated postulates, model declarations, hypotheses and
  mathematics; none of them is an observation.
- *No observations.* The page reports no experiment: it contains no apparatus,
  no calibration, no sample, no count, no uncertainty budget and no measured
  cross section. Nothing on the page should be read as a measurement of $V$,
  $\kappa$, a phase shift or a resonance parameter.
- *What a comparison would require.* To compare the model quantities
  $d\sigma/d\Omega$ or $\sigma$ with data one needs a declared target
  preparation (target density and composition), an incident fluence with its
  own uncertainty, a stated scattering geometry, a detector acceptance and
  efficiency model, and a background model, together with a declared
  statistical model for the counts. The equal-channel elastic flux assumptions
  of the beam model ([[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]]
  clause (d)) must be justified for the particular apparatus; inelastic or
  multichannel processes lie outside the model and would require separate
  channels.
- *Interpretation.* Agreement of a measured count rate with the model reading
  is evidence for the combined model-plus-apparatus assumptions; it is not a
  deduction that the declared model, its potential class or the framework
  describes nature. Disagreement would not by itself falsify the whole
  framework, and a finite dataset can be compatible with a model without
  confirming it.

**Scope of the model declarations.** The potential is prescribed, not derived;
the Coulomb coupling $\kappa$ and the resonance parameters $E_{r},\Gamma$ are
model parameters, not measured constants; and the modified Dollard comparison
of the Coulomb model is a declared construction whose phase convention changes
only asymptotic channel phases
([[def-nrqm-scattering-coulomb-dollard-model]] clauses (c), (d)).

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 12.3 printed pages 264-270 (PDF pages 272-278): cross sections and scattering experiments, the relation between the scattering amplitude and the measured count rate

items.physical_scope: The scope and empirical status of the three-dimensional scattering page: the distinction between the page's model deductions (existence, completeness, stationary amplitude, cross-section readings, Born and resonance models) and any observation; the apparatus and statistical qualifications needed before any measured count cross section could be compared with the model quantities; and the explicit absence of measured data on this page.

items.title: Long-range, threshold and model-scope limits of the scattering page
items.statement:
## Remarks

- **Long-range tails.** The short-range classes of
  [[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clause (b) exclude the
  pure Coulomb tail: the decaying-tail criterion of
  [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-resolvent-tail-asymptotic-completeness]] clause (c)
  requires a positive power $\delta>0$, and the Coulomb quotient
  $(1+|x|)^{1+\delta}|V(x)|$ is unbounded for every $\delta>0$. The general resolvent-tail exclusion follows from clause (d) of that same theorem: its translated compact-bump input gives $h(r)\ge C/(2r+R)$ with $C>0$, which is not integrable. The Coulomb
  case is treated by the modified Dollard comparison
  ([[def-nrqm-scattering-coulomb-dollard-model]]), for which the ordinary
  short-range comparison is not claimed.
- **Threshold.** The completeness statements of this page are made for the
  declared classes and do not require a zero-energy nonresonance hypothesis
  ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-resolvent-tail-short-range-completeness]]).
  A different uniformity statement fails at zero energy: for compactly
  supported potentials the scattering defects are not compact uniformly when
  the energy cutoff does not vanish at $0$
  ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-compact-scattering-defects]]). The general stationary beam and amplitude theorems use $k>0$ and give no uniform zero-energy amplitude statement. The companion's declared square-well computation separately proves its explicit zero-energy resonance profile.
- **Positive eigenvalues.** The absence of positive eigenvalues is part of
  [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-wave-operator-existence-and-free-continuity]] clause
  (d) for the compact-support class; no statement is made about negative or
  zero eigenvalues of the interacting operator, and no general bound-state inventory belongs to this page. The companion's explicit well has a separately proved local threshold branch, without a bound-state count for arbitrary potentials.
- **Resonances.** The resonance model
  ([[def-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-model]]) is a declared
  conditional model; the page proves no existence of a resonance for any
  declared potential and makes no analytic-continuation claim for the
  resolvent or the scattering operator.

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 12.4 printed pages 271-275 (PDF pages 279-283): the shielded Coulomb potential and the caution that a pure 1/r tail requires separate treatment

items.physical_scope: The explicit limits of the scattering page: the exclusion of the Coulomb tail from the short-range classes and its separate modified-comparison treatment, the threshold obstruction for uniform compact-defect statements at zero energy and the fact that completeness itself is unaffected, the absence of any zero-energy stationary statement, and the conditional status of the resonance model. This records scope; it asserts no new mathematical consequence.

items.title: S-wave phase shift of a declared spherical square well, with its low-energy limit and hard-sphere comparison
items.statement:
**Setup.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and declare the **spherical square well**
$$V(x):=\begin{cases}-U,&|x|<a,\\ 0,&|x|\ge a,\end{cases}\qquad U>0,\ a>0,$$
read in joules and metres; $V$ is real, bounded and compactly supported, so it
is in the compact-support class. Adopt the central stationary reading at wave
number $k>0$ of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] and the
$s$-wave ($l=0$) channel. Put
$$K:=\frac{\sqrt{2m(E+U)}}{\hbar},\qquad k:=\frac{\sqrt{2mE}}{\hbar},\qquad E>0 .$$
Because the declared potential is constant on each of the two regions and
bounded, the reduced radial function $u_0:=\varphi_0$ of the cited channel
vocabulary (up to a nonzero real normalization) is $C^1$ at $r=a$
with second derivative given by the reduced equation on each side, and the
$s$-wave phase shift is determined by matching: $u_{0}\propto\sin(Kr)$ for
$r<a$ and $u_{0}\propto\sin(kr+\delta_{0})$ for $r>a$.

The phase is read modulo $\pi$. For $z=X+iY\ne0$, $\arg z$ means an angle $\theta$ modulo $2\pi$ with $\cos\theta=X/|z|$ and $\sin\theta=Y/|z|$; hence $\arg z$ modulo $\pi$ determines the phase without dividing by $X$ or $Y$. Big-$O$ terms below are for $k\to0^+$ at a fixed depth and radius; depth comparisons are taken after that low-energy limit.

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Sections 15.5-15.6 printed pages 217-219: phase shifts and hard-sphere scattering, including the low-energy limit tan delta_l = -(ka)^(2l+1)/((2l+1)[(2l-1)!!]^2) and the total cross section 4 pi a^2
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 12.5.1 printed pages 279-281 (PDF pages 287-289): scattering at low energy and the s-wave dominance

items.physical_scope: A declared idealised spherical square well of depth U>0 and radius a in the central stationary scattering reading, at every positive energy E: nondividing s-wave matching, the finite-scattering-length and exact zero-energy-resonance branches, the associated onset of an s-wave bound-state branch at each threshold, and the hard-sphere comparison along nonresonant depth regimes and at matching nodes. The U=0 free case is also checked. No measured phase shift, measurement or material-target identification is asserted.

items.title: Born amplitude of a declared uniform ball potential with an explicit weak-coupling condition
items.statement:
**Setup.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$ and the **uniform ball potential**
$$V(x):=\begin{cases}V_{0},&|x|<R,\\ 0,&|x|\ge R,\end{cases}\qquad V_{0}\in\mathbb R,\ R>0,$$
read in joules and metres; adopt the stationary beam model at wave number
$k>0$ and direction $d$, and let $W=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$, $q=\|K_{k}\|$, $f_{k}$
and the Born amplitude $f_{B}$ be as in
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-controlled-born-approximation]]. Write
$\theta$ for the scattering angle, $\cos\theta=\Omega\cdot d$, and
$\mathbf q_{\mathrm{tr}}:=k(d-\Omega)$ for the wave-vector transfer and $q_{\mathrm{tr}}:=|\mathbf q_{\mathrm{tr}}|=2k\sin(\theta/2)$ for its magnitude.

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Section 15.4 printed pages 213-215: the Born approximation and the condition for its validity
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 12.4 printed pages 271-275 (PDF pages 279-283): scattering off a charge distribution with the Fourier transform of the potential

items.physical_scope: The declared short-range scattering model with a uniform real ball potential of strength V_0 and radius R in the pair's stationary beam reading: the explicit Born amplitude as a function of the momentum transfer, its forward value, and an explicit Hilbert-Schmidt condition on V_0, R and m that makes the controlled Born error estimate of the pair applicable. Conditional on the declared model and cited mathematics; no measured cross section and no claim that the Born reading applies outside the stated explicit condition.

items.title: A Yukawa tail satisfies the resolvent-tail class while the Coulomb limit does not
items.statement:
**Setup.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and declare the **Yukawa potential**
$$V_{g,\mu}(x):=-g\,\frac{e^{-\mu|x|}}{|x|}\qquad(x\ne0),\qquad g>0,\ \mu>0,$$
with the origin convention $V_{g,\mu}(0):=0$, read in joules, with $g$ in
$\mathrm{J\,m}$ and $\mu$ in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$. Fix the model's reference length $L_*>0$ and write $\mu_*:=\mu L_*>0$, a dimensionless screening parameter.

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Section 15.4 printed pages 214-215: the Yukawa potential reducing to the Coulomb potential as the screening parameter tends to zero
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 12.4 printed pages 271-275 (PDF pages 279-283): scattering off hydrogen with a shielded Coulomb potential

items.physical_scope: The declared short-range scattering model with a Yukawa (screened Coulomb) potential of coupling g>0 and screening parameter mu>0: the explicit split into a compactly supported square-integrable part and a bounded exponentially decaying tail, the verification that the tail satisfies the decaying-tail hypothesis of the resolvent-tail class, hence asymptotic completeness of the model, and the failure of that hypothesis in the unscreened Coulomb limit mu=0, whose treatment belongs to the declared long-range model. Conditional on the declared model and cited mathematics; no measured screening length, coupling or cross section is asserted.

items.title: Scope of the scattering examples page
items.statement:
## Remarks

- **Status of the examples.** Every item on this companion page is an
  idealised setup with a complete verification inside the declared model:
  the square well of
  [[ex-nrqm-scattering-square-well-s-wave-phase-shift]], the declared
  resonance factor of
  [[ex-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-cross-section]], the uniform
  ball Born amplitude of
  [[ex-nrqm-scattering-born-uniform-ball-amplitude]], and the Yukawa class
  check of
  [[ex-nrqm-scattering-long-range-tail-and-coulomb-warning]]. None is a
  reported experiment: there is no apparatus, calibration, sample, count or
  uncertainty budget on this page, and no number appearing here is a measured
  value.
- **Symbolic parameters.** The depth and radius of the well, the resonance
  energy and width, the ball strength and radius, and the Yukawa coupling and
  screening parameter remain symbolic throughout; the examples verify
  identities and class memberships, and assert no numerical value of $m$ or
  $\hbar$.
- **No extrapolation.** The hard-sphere comparison of the square-well example
  is a limit inside the declared family of wells; the low-energy limit is
  taken for the exact phase shift of the declared well and is not asserted as
  a universal low-energy law. The failures and limits recorded in the Yukawa
  example are statements about the declared potential class, not about any
  material target.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Chapter 12 printed pages 257-284 (PDF pages 265-292): the scattering chapter whose idealised models the examples instantiate
